title: QUIC RFC 9000 Initial Stream Limit Transport Parameters
purpose: Describe the RFC 9000 Section 18.2 floor for initial_max_streams_bidi and initial_max_streams_uni transport-parameter encoding and runtime stream-open gating.
design_summary: The transport-parameter codec represents initial_max_streams_bidi and initial_max_streams_uni as independent QUIC variable-length integer fields with parameter IDs 0x08 and 0x09. Values up to the 2^60 stream-count boundary are accepted, values above that boundary are rejected, and formatting preserves each value in its corresponding parameter. Runtime peer transport-parameter commit applies the parsed values as the initial peer bidirectional and unidirectional stream-open limits. When a parameter is absent or zero, the corresponding local stream type remains blocked and reports a STREAMS_BLOCKED frame until a later MAX_STREAMS frame increases that limit.
data_and_state_considerations: Null parsed stream-limit parameters mean absent transport parameters and are mapped to an initial peer stream-open limit of zero. Explicit zero values are preserved as zero. The bidirectional and unidirectional counters are separate: client bidirectional stream IDs advance by 4 from 0, and client unidirectional stream IDs advance by 4 from 2. MAX_STREAMS frames remain the only later mechanism in this slice for raising the corresponding peer stream-open limit.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The codec accepts exactly 2^60 as the stream-count boundary and rejects 2^60 + 1.
A missing initial_max_streams_bidi parameter blocks local bidirectional stream opens until a bidirectional MAX_STREAMS frame increases the limit.
An explicit zero initial_max_streams_bidi value blocks local bidirectional stream opens.
A missing initial_max_streams_uni parameter blocks local unidirectional stream opens until a unidirectional MAX_STREAMS frame increases the limit.
An explicit zero initial_max_streams_uni value blocks local unidirectional stream opens.
Bidirectional and unidirectional transport-parameter values do not overwrite each other.
risks: This slice covers initial stream-count transport parameters and local stream-open gating only; broader flow-control, scheduling, public stream APIs, and STREAMS_BLOCKED emission cadence remain owned by their existing requirements.
The tests use the managed stream-state seam and do not claim hosted interop behavior.
The benchmark suite already covers transport-parameter parser and formatter hot paths; this slice does not introduce a new benchmark scenario.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the bounded S18P2 stream-count transport-parameter floor for initial_max_streams_bidi, initial_max_streams_uni, and the absent-or-zero stream-open gate. It does not claim initial data-limit parameters, disable_active_migration, preferred_address fields, max_ack_delay policy, public APIs, or interop readiness.
